claims.text: High-entropy alloys possess intrinsic lattice distortions arising from chemical complexity.
These lattice distortions act as heterogeneous barriers to dislocation motion.
Under dynamic loading, lattice distortions promote a higher work-hardening rate than in conventional alloys.
Under dynamic loading, lattice distortions delay localized plasticity relative to conventional alloys.
The proposed high-entropy alloy is a uniform solid solution with local chemical fluctuations.
Its conventional-alloy control has lower chemical complexity and minimal lattice distortion.
Chemical disorder and atomic-size mismatch induce nanoscale lattice distortions.
Dynamic loading amplifies heterogeneous internal stress fields associated with lattice distortions.
The amplified internal stress fields impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases work hardening.
Impeded dislocation motion delays localized deformation and improves the balance of strength and ductility.
The high-entropy alloy will have greater strain-rate sensitivity than the conventional-alloy baseline.
The high-entropy alloy will exhibit a delayed onset of plasticity relative to the conventional-alloy baseline.
The hypothesis applies to single-phase solid-solution high-entropy alloys under dynamic loading at room to moderate temperatures when deformation is dislocation-mediated.
The hypothesis may not apply to multiphase systems or when alternative deformation mechanisms dominate.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field calls the control similar in overall composition but lower in chemical complexity, whereas the baseline describes it as having a simpler composition. Without a defined matching strategy, the proposed control cannot clearly vary chemical complexity while retaining similar overall composition.

The hypothesis and falsification measurements concern delayed localized plasticity or necking, but the predicted outcome instead says delayed onset of plasticity, which ordinarily refers to yielding and is not equivalent to delayed localization.
